why: The new examples pushed the model to keep larger predicate-attached spans (fewer cuts inside long NP/postmodifiers), which helps long-piece H_set, but also made it over-sensitive to short scope-bearing tokens and function words so it began producing singleton cuts (e.g. isolating "they've" / "not"), hurting short/mid bins — net effect small and mixed.
lesson: Later revisions should preserve the preference to keep predicate-attached spans intact while avoiding examples that can be read as encouraging single-token cuts of auxiliaries/negation or other function words.
blamed: E3 (intended to penalize function-word fragments but misgeneralized)
